back: The energy required to remove one electron from each atom in one mole of gaseous atoms to form one mole of gaseous 1+ ions.

front: Equation for the second ionisation energy of an element X?

back: Nuclear charge; distance of the electron from the nucleus (radius); shielding by inner electrons; spin-pair repulsion.

front: Why does first IE decrease down a group?
back: Extra shell: outer electron further away and more shielded; this outweighs the increased nuclear charge.

front: Why is the first IE of Al lower than Mg?
back: Al's outer electron is in 3p (higher energy, shielded by 3s) while Mg's is in 3s.

front: Why is the first IE of S lower than P?
back: S has a paired 3p electron; spin-pair repulsion makes it easier to remove. P's three 3p electrons are unpaired.

front: What does a big jump in successive ionisation energies show?
back: The next electron is removed from an inner shell (closer to the nucleus, less shielded). Electrons before the jump = outer-shell electrons = group.

front: Why does each successive ionisation energy increase?
back: Each electron is removed from a more positive ion: same nuclear charge, fewer electrons, less repulsion, smaller ion.
